title: Meta Ads vs Google Ads for D2C Brands in India (2026): Which to Start With and How to Split Budget

seoMeta.title: Meta Ads vs Google Ads for D2C Brands in India (2026)
seoMeta.description: Meta Ads or Google Ads first? A practical 2026 guide for Indian D2C brands: how to choose by demand type, split budget and fix tracking before you scale.
keywords: Meta Ads vs Google Ads India

summary: Start with Google Search if people already search for what you sell. Start with Meta Ads if your product is new, visual or impulse-led. A practical guide on demand types, budget splitting, and operational scaling for Indian D2C brands.
content:
By Vedant Tiwari, Senior Performance Marketer & Media Planner, Mumbai · Updated 26 November 2026 · 9 min read

**Short answer:** Start with Google Search if people already search for what you sell. Start with Meta Ads if your product is new, visual or impulse-led and you have to create demand first. Most Indian D2C brands eventually run both: Meta creates demand, Google captures it. A sensible opening split is roughly 70/30 in favour of the platform that matches your demand type, then adjust after three to four weeks of real data.

## Key takeaways

- Meta Ads is a demand-creation channel; Google Search is a demand-capture channel.
- Pick your first platform by demand type, not by habit or by what competitors do.
- Fix tracking (Meta Conversions API, GA4 and GTM) before scaling spend on either platform.
- Judge each channel on blended results and cost per qualified outcome, not on in-platform ROAS alone.
- Kill weak ad sets early and test creative daily. This is what moved cost per result in the case below.

## Meta Ads vs Google Ads at a glance

| Lever | Meta Ads (Facebook + Instagram) | Google Ads (Search + Shopping + Performance Max) |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Core job | Create demand | Capture existing demand |
| User intent | Low to medium (scrolling) | High (searching) |
| Best for | New, visual or impulse products; launches; app installs | Products people already search for; branded and category terms |
| Main lever | Creative and audience signals | Keywords, intent and feed quality |
| Speed to first sales | Fast with strong creative | Fast if search volume exists |
| Typical risk | Creative fatigue | Paying for low-intent or irrelevant queries |

## How to decide which platform to start with

Ask three questions.

**1. Do people already search for this?** Check Google Keyword Planner and Google Trends for your product and category terms. If there is steady search volume, Google Search and Shopping should be live from week one. If almost nobody searches for it, Google has little to capture and Meta should lead.

**2. Is the product visual or emotional?** Fashion, home decor, food, gifting and travel tend to do well on Meta because a scroll-stopping Reel can sell the idea. Utility products people research before buying lean towards Google.

**3. What is your average order value and margin?** Low-margin, low-AOV products can struggle with high-intent keyword costs. High-AOV products can justify them. Work out your break-even ROAS before you spend a rupee on either platform.

## How to split your budget by stage

These are starting heuristics, not industry benchmarks. Your own data should overrule them.

| Stage | Meta Ads | Google Ads | Why |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| New brand, new category | 70% | 30% | Demand has to be created first |
| Established category, brand starting out | 40% | 60% | Searchers already exist; capture them |
| Scaling brand with proven creative | 50% | 50% | Meta feeds the funnel, Google closes it |
| Heavy festive season push (Diwali, Raksha Bandhan) | Raise Meta share temporarily | Protect branded search | Festive CPMs rise, so creative quality matters more |

Keep a protected slice for branded search on Google. Cheap brand clicks often get cannibalised when Performance Max is left unchecked.

## Tracking comes before scale

Neither platform can optimise on data it cannot see. Before scaling:

1. **Meta Pixel plus server-side Conversions API (CAPI).** Browser-only tracking loses conversions to iOS privacy settings and ad blockers.
2. **GA4 with Google Tag Manager.** Set up purchase events, custom dimensions and cross-domain measurement correctly.
3. **One source of truth.** Compare platform-reported numbers with your store backend. Platforms over-report because both claim credit for the same sale.
4. **Clear conversion definitions.** Count purchases or qualified leads, not clicks or page views.

## Real example: lowering cost per result on Meta Ads

For CURA, an AI travel-tech platform, we brought the cost per result on Meta Ads down from ₹278 to ₹149, a 46% reduction, while growing daily conversions. The levers were operational, not magical:

- Pausing ad sets that kept spending without results
- Consolidating budget into the ad sets that were working
- Shipping fresh UGC-style Reels daily instead of waiting for fatigue to show
- Segmenting audiences by city tier

Read the full breakdown: [How We Scaled CURA on Meta Ads](https://vedantverse.in/blog/how-we-scaled-cura-meta-ads-cost-per-result).

## Common mistakes that waste budget

- **Running both platforms with no tracking.** You will not know which one worked.
- **Judging Meta like Google.** Meta users are not searching. Expect a longer, softer path to purchase.
- **Letting Performance Max run unsupervised.** Use brand exclusions, asset-group structure and product-margin segmentation.
- **Changing too much at once.** Edit one variable at a time or you cannot learn what moved the result.
- **Starving the learning phase.** Meta's guidance is roughly 50 optimisation events per ad set per week. Spreading a small budget across too many ad sets prevents this.

## A simple 30-60-90 day plan

**Days 1-30: Foundations.** Fix tracking, define break-even ROAS, launch the platform that matches your demand type, and test 4 to 6 creatives or keyword themes.

**Days 31-60: Learn and cut.** Pause the bottom performers, double down on winners, and add the second platform at 20 to 30% of budget.

**Days 61-90: Scale carefully.** Raise budgets in steady steps, add retargeting and Shopping or Performance Max, and review blended CAC against margin.

## Frequently asked questions

### Is Meta Ads or Google Ads better for a new D2C brand in India?

It depends on demand type. If people already search for your product, start with Google Search and Shopping. If you are creating a new category or selling a visual, impulse-led product, start with Meta Ads. Most brands end up using both.

### How much should a D2C brand spend on Meta and Google Ads?

Start with enough budget to gather meaningful data, then split roughly 70/30 towards the platform that matches your demand type. Adjust after three to four weeks based on blended cost per acquisition and margin, not on platform-reported ROAS alone.

### Why does Meta Ads report more conversions than my store shows?

Platforms use their own attribution windows and often both claim credit for the same sale. Implement Conversions API, use GA4 as a neutral check, and compare against actual orders in your store backend.

### Should I run Performance Max or Search first?

Start with Search for brand and high-intent category keywords so you control the queries. Add Performance Max once you have conversion data and a clean product feed, with brand exclusions in place.

### How long before I know if my ads are working?

Give each test two to four weeks, or enough conversions to exit Meta's learning phase. Judging a campaign in three days usually leads to bad decisions.
